Q1.population: job seekers offered coaching in 2025 and 2026
Q1.comparison: no coaching for the same seekers
Q1.outcome: employed within six months of registration
Q1.summary: average effect on the offered (ATT), a difference in employment rates

Q2.treatment: an allocation rule that offers one place per five seekers
Q2.comparison: current caseworker practice, and other rules within the same budget
Q2.summary: policy value: the employment rate if the rule decided, and its gain over current practice

Q3.treatment: places to the top fifth by conditional effect of coaching
Q3.comparison: places to the top fifth by risk score
Q3.summary: difference in policy value between the two rankings, same budget

answer: The risk score finds the seekers least likely to find work without help, but in the pilot those seekers gain about 10 points from coaching, against 24 points for the fifth who gain most; only 24% of the two groups are the same people. Risk is the outcome without coaching, benefit is the difference coaching makes, so places should follow estimated benefit, which we estimate and check on Day 2.
